correctness.rationale: For the full algebraically closed smooth Picard family, exact universal coefficients in F7[a,b,c] give a one-dimensional Cartier block 2a and a two-dimensional block with recorded entries. Zero stable rank forces a=0,b≠0. The rank-one block has zero Cartier square iff c(2b^8+3c^6)=0; the discriminant b^4(4t-6) excludes the singular t=5 of the t∈{2,5} solutions. All and only t=0,2 remain smooth; rank of Cartier is 1, a-number 2. Bouw et al. Lemmas 1.17 and 1.21 imply exactly two nonspecial abstract isomorphism classes. The packaged pure-Python verifier replayed universal coefficients and a full GF343 normalized census. No finite test is substituted for the universal argument.

originality.rationale: The classical t=0 curve and the normal-form/isomorphism machinery are prior work. This theorem identifies the additional t=2 isomorphism class and proves exhaustiveness among all smooth geometric genus-three Picard curves in characteristic seven. The apparent general a-number zero assertion of Nourozi–Rahmati at p≡1 mod3 is explicitly refuted by a smooth example within its hypothesis, rather than accepted as stronger coverage. Targeted published-index, public claim-record, and primary-literature comparisons found no correct complete two-class theorem, with clearly stated residual 2015 full-text and unindexed-work risks.

value.rationale: The rank-zero stratum of genus-three cyclic triple covers is a natural arithmetic moduli locus of finite expected size in characteristic seven. Determining exactly two abstract geometric curve classes, their common a-number, and the singular boundary is a complete classification with reuse value for Picard Jacobians, not a randomly chosen coefficient slice. The second class is absent from the earlier individually studied classical CM model, and it provides a substantive explicit counterexample to a broad published a-number claim.
